spec_match.rationale: All four radius keywords are resolved with the exact CSS Shapes 1 geometry (side min/max, corner hypot), and the clip uses the real circle(<keyword> at x y) declaration when the browser parses it.

interactive.rationale: Centre sliders and four aria-pressed keyword buttons drive a live clipped stage, an SVG geometry overlay, and a per-keyword radius table that all update on input.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb and the stage heading both say 'drag the centre', but there is no pointer drag on the frame — the centre only moves via the two range sliders.

edge_cases.rationale: Unsupported-browser fallback and all four keywords are covered, but ellipse() — half of the feature's title and asserted in the conformance suite — is never demonstrated with its two independent radii, and centre-outside-the-box behaviour is unexplored.

references.rationale: See-also links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5100672946143232 and the CSS Shapes 1 basic-shape-functions section.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves circle/ellipse corner keywords across clip-path, shape-outside and offset-path, pins the radial-gradient parity baseline, keeps side keywords, and rejects the invented nearest-corner negative.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: exercised cx slider to 80% and the closest-corner button; readout recomputed (fallback clip circle(153.3px at 80% 40%)), aria-pressed state moved, table re-rendered; console clean, zero exceptions, only the environment's proxied Google Fonts request failed; desktop+mobile screenshots captured.

telemetry_health.rationale: Every render emits a console line and showcaseTelemetry.assert('keyword-resolved', …) with keyword, centre, radius and support flag; no runtime errors observed.

design_system.rationale: Colours are CSS variables throughout, the keyword buttons set background and color together in both states, and the page is a live lab rather than a static card.

accessibility.rationale: Sliders are labelled with visible value spans, keyword toggles are real buttons with aria-pressed, the results table has caption/scope, the SVG overlay is aria-hidden, and the summary readout is an aria-live output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP at 360x740 DPR3 touch and 1280x800: documentElement.scrollWidth equals innerWidth on both (0px overflow), controls are min-height 44px, and both screenshots render legibly with no clipped content.

openQuestions.title: Make the centre actually draggable, or stop saying 'drag'
openQuestions.detail: The lede says 'drag the shape's centre around its box' and the stage heading is 'Drag the centre', but the frame accepts no pointer input — the centre only moves through two range sliders. Either add a pointerdown/pointermove handler on #frame that maps to the cx/cy values (keeping the sliders as the keyboard path) or reword the copy. Consult modern-web-guidance for touch drag + keyboard-equivalent patterns before implementing.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate ellipse() with two independently keyworded radii
openQuestions.detail: The feature is titled for circle() AND ellipse(), and the conformance suite asserts ellipse(closest-corner farthest-corner …) parses, yet no concept in the portfolio ever renders an ellipse or shows what mixing keywords per axis does. A page that lets the user pick each radius keyword independently and visualises the per-axis corner distances would cover the second half of the shipped surface.

summary: Solid lab: real keyword geometry, honest Chromium-141 fallback banner (corner keywords in basic shapes are a v155 surface and correctly reported unsupported), clean console, and full mobile/desktop parity measured over CDP. Verified on http://localhost:3000/v155/closest-corner-and-farthest-corner-radii-for-circle-and-ellipse-basic-shapes/keyword-lab/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; headless CDP + screenshot read is the sanctioned path here). Feature /conformance/ route executed 3 pass / 5 fail, the failures being genuine pre-155 browser gaps. Gaps: the 'drag' copy oversells the input, and ellipse() is undemonstrated portfolio-wide.
